entities.name: Kagemni
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kagemni was a pivotal vizier during the nascent years of the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt, serving under its founder, King Teti (c. 2345–2323 BCE). His career marked a crucial period of administrative consolidation following the Fifth Dynasty, underscoring the growing power and sophistication of the vizierate as a central pillar of pharaonic governance. His monumental mastaba at Saqqara, replete with elaborate reliefs detailing daily life and his official duties, provides invaluable archaeological evidence for the social and economic structures of the Old Kingdom.

As vizier, Kagemni held the highest administrative office, overseeing justice, treasury, agriculture, and public works for the entire Two Lands. His tenure likely involved implementing policies aimed at stabilizing royal authority and managing the vast resources of the state. The detailed scenes within his tomb depict him supervising granaries, fishing expeditions, and craft workshops, illustrating the diverse responsibilities of his office. He was also 'Chief Justice' and 'Overseer of all Royal Works', indicating his comprehensive control over both legal and construction projects.

Kagemni's administrative contributions, alongside those of contemporary viziers like Mereruka, helped to define the role of the vizierate for subsequent dynasties, establishing precedents for bureaucratic organization that would persist for centuries. The grandeur of his tomb, second only to the pharaoh's own, also reflected and perhaps further propelled the trend of high officials accumulating significant wealth and prestige, a development that would eventually challenge central royal power towards the end of the Old Kingdom. His funerary complex thus serves as a tangible record of the increasing decentralization of power.
